note: t.Skip/Skipf/SkipNow call sites per package, outside internal/testenv. A COUNT rather than a per-site registry: a registry needs an entry for every one of these, most of which are honest environmental skips, and a list that long becomes a rubber stamp. This can only fall on regeneration; raising it is a hand edit of this file.

raisedBy.why: The upload probe gate needs a real ffprobe to gate with and a real ffmpeg to build media to feed it, and neither is a property of the code. The six sites are: ffprobeOrSkip (no ffprobe, so there is nothing to gate with); sampleMedia's two (no ffmpeg, and an ffmpeg that cannot mux h264/aac); buildSample's one (same, for internal/ffmpeg); and TWO Windows ones -- TestProbeFileReturnsWhenItsContextIsCancelled, whose fixture is a #!/bin/sh wrapper script chosen precisely because it leaves a grandchild holding the stdout pipe, and internal/api's fakeProbe, which is the same shape and which Windows will not execute. Every one is 'this environment cannot run the test', none is 'the thing under test changed'.
raisedBy.alreadyPaidDown: The first draft of the same tests added ELEVEN sites. sampleMedia and buildSample were extracted so that each environmental reason has exactly one site for the whole file instead of one per test, which also took two pre-existing per-test build skips with it. See issue #187: the real fix is making these fail rather than skip when POLYEMESIS_REQUIRE_FFMPEG is set in CI, at which point the four FFmpeg ones can come back out. The two Windows ones need a different fix -- a small helper binary built by the test instead of a shell script -- and are issue #190.

raisedBy.why: The normalise worker now re-runs internal/ffmpeg.ProbeFile's format allowlist on its source before it transcodes anything, which is the SECOND gate an upload the client kept the server from inspecting has to get past. The test that proves an ffconcat script cannot get past it needs a real ffprobe to gate with and a real ffmpeg to build the media the script names, and neither is a property of the code. ONE site, realMediaOrSkip, naming all three environmental reasons at once (no ffmpeg, no ffprobe, an ffmpeg that cannot mux h264/aac); three separate ones would be three free passes for the same condition.
raisedBy.alreadyPaidDown: The same round added a Finding-B test to internal/ffmpeg with two more environmental reasons -- a build that cannot mux AIFF/y4m/GIF, and a build that puts one of them on the allowlist -- and neither is a skip. They log and return, and the parent asserts that at least one of the three formats reached the branch under test, which is a stronger statement than three skips could make. internal/api's new tests added none: they reuse the existing fakeProbe and ffprobeOrSkip sites. Issues #187 and #190 still cover turning the remaining FFmpeg and Windows ones into failures.

loweredBy.why: #187, which the raisedBy entry above named as the real fix and deferred. ffprobeOrSkip (internal/api) and needFFmpeg (internal/ffmpeg) now call internal/testenv.FFmpegBinary, which SKIPS on a machine without the binary and FAILS, naming it, when POLYEMESIS_REQUIRE_FFMPEG is set -- which .github/workflows/ci.yml's go job now does. The two skip calls moved into internal/testenv, which this census excludes by design, so the count falls by two. Capability skips are deliberately untouched: an ffmpeg that cannot mux h264/aac is still an environment fact in CI, and only a binary's outright absence is a defect.
loweredBy.notPaidDown: The two Windows sites are still #190 and still skips, and sampleMedia's capability skips are still skips. This entry lowers the ratchet rather than closing the class.
loweredBy.handEditedRatherThanRegenerated: `go test ./internal/testenv -run TestNoNewBareSkipCanLand -update-skips` produces exactly these numbers and DELETES the raisedBy array above on the way past: skipCensus has no field for it, so writeSkipCensus round-trips the file through a struct that cannot see it. The written reasons are the entire reviewable half of this ratchet, so the three numbers were lowered by hand instead. Filed as a finding on the same round that filed #205, which is the same shape one artifact over.

raisedBy2.why: Raw elementary streams (.h264/.hevc/.mpegvideo) are now accepted with a COUNTED length instead of refused, and testing that needs a real raw bitstream, which only a real encoder can produce. THREE of the four are the same environmental reason once per package: an FFmpeg without libx264/libx265/mpeg2video cannot write the fixture at all. They are capability skips of exactly the shape #187 left in place -- a binary's outright absence fails under POLYEMESIS_REQUIRE_FFMPEG via testenv.FFmpegBinary, which all three fixtures route through first; only 'this build lacks that encoder' skips. The FOURTH is internal/ffmpeg's TestACountThatWasCutShortIsNotAVerdictAboutTheFile, which stands a #!/bin/sh script in for ffmpeg so a cancellation lands inside the count with no wall-clock budget anywhere in the test. That is #190's class exactly, and the same shape as TestProbeFileReturnsWhenItsContextIsCancelled three functions away.
raisedBy2.alreadyPaidDown: The first draft added SEVEN sites; four were removed before this was written. internal/playlistmedia's fixture hand-rolled two exec.LookPath skips, which are now one testenv.FFmpegBinary call each and so leave the census entirely; internal/api's did the same for ffmpeg. internal/ffmpeg's TestACountedLengthIsNotReportedAsADeclaredOne remuxes the raw stream to MPEG-TS with -c copy, which involves no encoder and therefore cannot fail on a build that just wrote the source -- that is a t.Fatalf, not a skip. The seven other new tests across the three packages added no sites: the three-format table in TestARawElementaryStreamIsAcceptedWithACountedDuration logs and counts instead of skipping per format, and asserts at the end that at least one format reached the branch, which the Finding-B entry above established as the stronger pattern.
raisedBy2.handEditedRatherThanRegenerated: For the reason the entry above records: -update-skips round-trips this file through a struct with no field for these reasons and deletes every one of them. The four numbers were raised by hand. Regenerating also silently drops internal/supervisor, whose count has fallen to zero; that is left alone here rather than swept into an unrelated change.
